# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*The following is Angular's official best-practices rules file, included verbatim from
<https://angular.dev/assets/context/best-practices.md>. It is part of the Angular
architecture.*

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

### Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angular v22+ and provide signal-based state, type-safe field access, and schema-based validation
- When not using Signal Forms, prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones
- Do NOT use `ngClass`, use `class` bindings instead
- Do NOT use `ngStyle`, use `style` bindings instead
- Do NOT import `CommonModule`, import only the directives and pipes the template uses, such as `AsyncPipe` or `DatePipe`
- When using external templates/styles, use paths relative to the component TS file.

## State Management

- Use signals for local component state
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Keep state transformations pure and predictable
- Do NOT use `mutate` on signals, use `update` or `set` instead

## Templates

- Keep templates simple and avoid complex logic
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) instead of `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`
- Use the async pipe to handle observables
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.

## Services

- Design services around a single responsibility
- Use the `providedIn: 'root'` option for singleton services
- Prefer the `@Service` decorator over `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` for new singleton services (Angular v22+)
- Use the `inject()` function instead of constructor injection

---

## Spring

This is a standard Spring Boot application, built with conventional Spring MVC
(`@RestController` request handling, a service layer, Spring Data / JPA persistence, and Bean
Validation). Follow ordinary Spring conventions and idioms throughout. Spring's reference
documentation is the guidance for the server: Spring Boot
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.1/reference/> and Spring Framework
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/>.

package net.officefloor.hq.app.settings;


/** An action the sheet's permission matrix decides who may take, with the roles that may take it when
 * the matrix leaves it blank. */
public enum Action {
    OPEN(EnumSet.of(Role.CLERK, Role.STEWARD)),
    SETTLE(EnumSet.of(Role.CLERK, Role.STEWARD)),
    VOID(EnumSet.of(Role.CLERK, Role.STEWARD)),
    REASSIGN(EnumSet.of(Role.STEWARD)),
    CLOSE(EnumSet.of(Role.CLERK, Role.STEWARD)),
    REOPEN(EnumSet.of(Role.STEWARD));

    private final Set<Role> standing;

    Action(Set<Role> standing) {
        this.standing = standing;
    }

    /** The roles that may take the action when the matrix leaves it blank. */
    public Set<Role> standing() {
        return standing;
    }

    /** The action's name as the settings show it: open, settle, and so on. */
    public String key() {
        return name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
    }
}

    VIEWER
}

I didn't change anything. One thing up front shapes the whole answer: **the screen works out every figure itself, in the browser.** The server's claim API (`ClaimController.ClaimView`) sends only the raw claim fields plus `settledDue` and `statedDue`. The screen then computes due amounts, totals and flags in `people.ts`, `claims.ts`, `rates.service.ts` and `claims.service.ts`. The server has its own copy of the same rules in `RollupService` and `ClaimService`, which it uses for settling, statements, closing periods and the audit lines (ROLLUP, TOTALS, ALERT).

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Per claim (`claims.ts`)
| testid | Rule |
|---|---|
| `claim-due` | Front end `claimShownCents`, server `shownOf`. A **frozen** claim (SETTLED, or VOID with a `settledDue`) shows `settledDue`. Otherwise it starts from the **figure** (`claimDueCents` / `figureOf`): the bound `statedDue` if a statement bound the claim and it isn't PENDING; else amount × the rate in force on the claim's date for the grade the person had on that date (`rateOn` / `RateChain`, which falls back to parent sheets up to `LEVELS_UP`). The shown due is `max(figure + lateCharge, floor in force on the claim's date)`. A correction gets neither the late charge nor the floor. With no rate it shows `n/a`. |
| late charge | `lateChargeCents` / `overdueChargeOf`. Only OPEN or PENDING claims that aren't deferred or corrections. For each full 30 days past `overdueFrom`, the late % in force on that boundary date applies to the figure plus earlier charges (it compounds). It is never bound by a statement; settling fixes it in. |
| rounding | `roundsHalfUp` / `roundingOf`. Half-up if the claim is dated before the policy date in force (the one set, else the sheet's today); half-even otherwise. A correction uses the date of the claim it corrects. |
| `claim-due-by` | `HolidayService.dueBy`: the `terms`-th business day after `dueFrom`, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays. Terms are fixed when the claim is added: the person's own, else the grade's terms in force on the claim's date, else the sheet's (default 14). A holiday added later recomputes due-by on claims that aren't SETTLED or VOID and fall on or after it. A re-date leaves due-by alone. |
| `claim-overdue` | `overdue`: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` is before today. `overdueFrom` is due-by plus the grade's grace days in force on the claim's date. |
| `claim-period` | The period whose dates contain the **due-by**, not the claim's date. |
| `claim-number` | Given when the claim is opened (`nextNumber`). If period numbering is on (`numbersByPeriod`), it's `<period>-n`, or `X-n` outside any period. Otherwise it's `FY<yyyy>-n`, shared across the sheet tree and following the fiscal start month. A number is never reused. A reassign gives a new number; void keeps it. |
| `claim-deferred` | OPEN and today is before `deferredUntil`. The screen also shows "yes" for a VOID claim whose deferral date is still ahead. |
| `claim-stated`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-batch`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-log-line` | Stored flags and values. A claim is a late entry if its due-by fell in a soft-closed period when it was added. Each log line records the shown due at that moment. |

### Per person (`people.ts`)
- **Which claims count** (`countsLive` / `countsAs`, written in both languages):
  - Only OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count.
  - An OPEN claim deferred on today doesn't count.
  - An OPEN or PENDING claim doesn't count if it is dated inside one of the person's holds (`isHeldOn(claim.date)`), or the person's retirement date has been reached (`isRetiredOn(today)`). A statement binding overrides both, except on a PENDING claim.
- `person-claimed`: sum of the amounts of counting claims, leaving out corrections. The comment in `claimedCentsOf` says "OPEN and SETTLED", but PENDING claims count too.
- `person-due-total` (`dueTotalOf` / `dueCentsOf`): sum of the shown dues of counting claims, then `min(sum, cap in force on today)`. It's `n/a` if no claim has a figure and the person's grade (as of today) has no rate today.
- `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` (`splitOf`): the same sum before the cap, split by status.
- `person-excess`: how far the uncapped sum is above the cap.
- `person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`: counting claims that are overdue.
- `person-aged-0-30`, `-31-60`, `-61`: counting OPEN and PENDING claims, bucketed by days from the claim's date to today.
- `person-active`: has a counting OPEN or PENDING claim dated in the last 30 days, today included.
- `person-period-<name>-due-total` (`personPeriodCents`):
  - While the period is open: claims whose due-by falls in it and that counted by their status at the end of the period's last day (`statusOn` / `statusAt`, read from the status log), valued at today's shown due.
  - Once closed or soft-closed: the per-person figure fixed at close (`Period.closedPersonTotals`). A person added later shows 0. A merge folds the merged person's figure into the other's; a person who leaves has theirs dropped.
- `person-backing`: patron shares are 100/n, rounded half-even, with the first-named patron taking the remainder. Backing is each patron's SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days × their share.
- `person-cut-total`: from `PoolService`. Cuts are pot × share among members with a cut, half-even, with the remainder going to the smallest non-zero cut. Retired members, and members on hold *on today*, get 0.00. An unbalanced pool has no cuts. Members whose membership dates exclude today are left out.
- `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date`: from the person's last statement.
- `person-retired`: "yes" as soon as any retirement date is set, even a future one. That same flag hides the person from the list and from the summary-by-grade, while the due-total only drops their open claims once the date is reached.
- `person-hold`: "yes" if the person has any hold at all.

### Sheet level
- `rollup-due-total`, `header-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-total`, `header-overdue-total`: per-person figures added up with **`trimmedSum`**, which leaves out the single highest and lowest when there are three or more people with a figure. A person whose due-total is `n/a` is skipped.
- `rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`, `rollup-cut-total`, `rollup-overdue-count`: plain sums, not trimmed. So settled + open won't generally equal the due total.
- `consolidated-*`: this sheet's own (trimmed) figures plus the descendant sheets' figures from `ConsolidatedService`.
- `my-due-total` / `my-overdue-total`: the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user.
- Summary (`summary.ts`):
  - By grade: people not retired, on their grade today, with uncapped-per-grade sums of their capped due-totals.
  - By period: due total and change from the previous period by start date.
  - By tag: a claim counts under its own tags and its person's tags, once per tag.
  - By month: by the claim's date.
  - Counts by status and by void reason.
- `period-due-total`: the sum of the per-person period figures.

### Rules for actions (`ClaimService` unless noted)
- **Status flow** (`ClaimStatus.canBecome`): DRAFT → OPEN, VOID or DELETED. OPEN → PENDING, SETTLED or VOID. PENDING → SETTLED (approve), OPEN (reject) or VOID. SETTLED → VOID. A deleted claim can be restored to DRAFT only on the same sheet-today it was deleted. Only DRAFT claims can be edited, and the editor lock holds only for that sheet-today.
- **Open:** refused if the note is empty and the due is above the note threshold in force on the claim's date. Also refused if the period cap on OPEN/PENDING claims per person (`refuseOverCap`) is already reached.
- **Settle:**
  - The user's role must be allowed by the permission matrix.
  - The user can't be the one who opened or last edited the claim (`isOpenedOrEditedBy`).
  - A deferred claim can't be settled.
  - With no proofs, the due must not be above the proof threshold: the grade's own, else the sheet's, in force on the claim's date.
  - A clerk settling a claim whose due is above the clerk limit in force on today makes it **PENDING** instead.
  - Otherwise `settledDue` is frozen as `liveDueOf(statedDue or dueOf)`: the bound figure if there is one, else the rate figure, plus the late charge and floor.
- **Approve and reject:** steward only, and approve can't be done by the opener or editor. Approve freezes the live figure (no statement binding).
- **Void of a SETTLED claim:** steward only, within 7 days of the first SETTLED log date. The audit records `reversed=`. While the sheet has a list of void reasons, a void must name one.
- **Resettle:** steward only. Re-freezes at `openShownOf`, i.e. what would be due now as an unbound OPEN claim.
- **Redate:** steward only, OPEN or PENDING claims. Due-by, number and binding stay.
- **Split:** OPEN, not deferred, 0 < amount < the claim's amount. The original claim loses its binding; the new claim gets new terms, due-by and number.
- **Reassign:** by permission matrix (steward by default). Not on SETTLED or VOID claims or corrections. The claim loses its binding and, if numbered, gets a new number.
- **Correction:** a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person, and only corrections may name one.
- **Retirement:** a claim can't be dated after `retiredFrom`, or strictly inside a past retirement (`requireClaimable`).
- **Closed period** (`refuseClosed` on due-by): blocks almost every claim change. Adding a proof is allowed.
- **Soft-close:** fixes the totals, but changes are still allowed and new claims are flagged as late entries.
- **Close, reopen, auto-close:** close and reopen follow the matrix (close: clerk or steward; reopen: steward). Auto-close (`closeOverdue`) runs when today changes, once the period's to-date plus the sheet's grace days has passed. Today changing also releases locks and writes a SNAPSHOT line per person.
- **Statement** (`StatementService.take`): binds each counting claim to its **figure** (without late charge or floor) and unbinds every other claim of the person. It records the due-total and count. It can be taken as of an earlier date, using `SheetAsOf` as the basis. Only a steward can cancel the last statement, which unbinds what it bound.
- **Roles:** `Role` is CLERK, STEWARD or VIEWER. `Action` defines the standing rules (OPEN, SETTLE, VOID, CLOSE: clerk or steward; REASSIGN, REOPEN: steward), and `SheetPermission` can override them. `DelegationService` makes a user a steward for a date range. Several things are hard-wired to the steward role: redate, resettle, approve, reject, late void, merge, transfer, clone, archive. `ViewerGuard`, `SheetArchivedGuard` and `AsOfGuard` refuse every write; bulk actions instead report each claim as refused.
- **Imports and bulk actions:**
  - Person import (`PersonImportService`): all-or-nothing. A matching name or alias updates that person, with the grade taking effect from today.
  - Rate import: all-or-nothing.
  - Claim paste: all-or-nothing, adds DRAFTs, and a trailing `#ref` in the note becomes the reference.
  - Quick-add: creates the person with grade A if new.
  - Plan generate: each claim is added on its own, and refused dates are retried next time.
  - Bulk settle: all-or-nothing, and creates a batch (BATCH_SETTLED).
  - Bulk open, move and redate: claim by claim.
- **Dated settings** (`DatedSettings`): defaults are floor 1.00, late 0.00%, terms 14. Floor, late %, terms and the proof and note thresholds use the value in force on the **claim's date**; the clerk limit and cap use the value on the **sheet's today**.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard. The server side is reasonably central and well commented: `RollupService` for the figures and `ClaimService` for the rules. But the figures the screen actually shows are **re-implemented in TypeScript**, spread over a 2,350-line `people.ts`, `rates.service.ts` and `claims.service.ts`. The same "counts / due / late charge / rounding / period-at-end" logic also appears in `PeriodService` and `StatementService`/`SheetAsOf`. So each rule exists two or three times, and a new developer has to cross-check them. That is how I found the small drifts noted above: the claimed-total comment, retired-flag vs retirement-date, and holds judged by claim date for totals but by today for pool cuts.

- `person-claimed`: sum of the amounts of counting claims, leaving out corrections. The comment in `claimedCentsOf` says "OPEN and SETTLED", but PENDING claims count too.
- `person-due-total` (`dueTotalOf` / `dueCentsOf`): sum of the shown dues of counting claims, then `min(sum, cap in force on today)`. It's `n/a` if no claim has a figure and the person's grade (as of today) has no rate today.
- `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` (`splitOf`): the same sum before the cap, split by status.
- `person-excess`: how far the uncapped sum is above the cap.
- `person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`: counting claims that are overdue.
- `person-aged-0-30`, `-31-60`, `-61`: counting OPEN and PENDING claims, bucketed by days from the claim's date to today.
- `person-active`: has a counting OPEN or PENDING claim dated in the last 30 days, today included.
- `person-period-<name>-due-total` (`personPeriodCents`):
  - While the period is open: claims whose due-by falls in it and that counted by their status at the end of the period's last day (`statusOn` / `statusAt`, read from the status log), valued at today's shown due.
  - Once closed or soft-closed: the per-person figure fixed at close (`Period.closedPersonTotals`). A person added later shows 0. A merge folds the merged person's figure into the other's; a person who leaves has theirs dropped.
- `person-backing`: patron shares are 100/n, rounded half-even, with the first-named patron taking the remainder. Backing is each patron's SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days × their share.
- `person-cut-total`: from `PoolService`. Cuts are pot × share among members with a cut, half-even, with the remainder going to the smallest non-zero cut. Retired members, and members on hold *on today*, get 0.00. An unbalanced pool has no cuts. Members whose membership dates exclude today are left out.
- `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date`: from the person's last statement.
- `person-retired`: "yes" as soon as any retirement date is set, even a future one. That same flag hides the person from the list and from the summary-by-grade, while the due-total only drops their open claims once the date is reached.
- `person-hold`: "yes" if the person has any hold at all.

### Sheet level
- `rollup-due-total`, `header-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-total`, `header-overdue-total`: per-person figures added up with **`trimmedSum`**, which leaves out the single highest and lowest when there are three or more people with a figure. A person whose due-total is `n/a` is skipped.
- `rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`, `rollup-cut-total`, `rollup-overdue-count`: plain sums, not trimmed. So settled + open won't generally equal the due total.
- `consolidated-*`: this sheet's own (trimmed) figures plus the descendant sheets' figures from `ConsolidatedService`.
- `my-due-total` / `my-overdue-total`: the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user.
- Summary (`summary.ts`):
  - By grade: people not retired, on their grade today, with uncapped-per-grade sums of their capped due-totals.
  - By period: due total and change from the previous period by start date.
  - By tag: a claim counts under its own tags and its person's tags, once per tag.
  - By month: by the claim's date.
  - Counts by status and by void reason.
- `period-due-total`: the sum of the per-person period figures.

### Rules for actions (`ClaimService` unless noted)
- **Status flow** (`ClaimStatus.canBecome`): DRAFT → OPEN, VOID or DELETED. OPEN → PENDING, SETTLED or VOID. PENDING → SETTLED (approve), OPEN (reject) or VOID. SETTLED → VOID. A deleted claim can be restored to DRAFT only on the same sheet-today it was deleted. Only DRAFT claims can be edited, and the editor lock holds only for that sheet-today.
- **Open:** refused if the note is empty and the due is above the note threshold in force on the claim's date. Also refused if the period cap on OPEN/PENDING claims per person (`refuseOverCap`) is already reached.
- **Settle:**
  - The user's role must be allowed by the permission matrix.
  - The user can't be the one who opened or last edited the claim (`isOpenedOrEditedBy`).
  - A deferred claim can't be settled.
  - With no proofs, the due must not be above the proof threshold: the grade's own, else the sheet's, in force on the claim's date.
  - A clerk settling a claim whose due is above the clerk limit in force on today makes it **PENDING** instead.
  - Otherwise `settledDue` is frozen as `liveDueOf(statedDue or dueOf)`: the bound figure if there is one, else the rate figure, plus the late charge and floor.
- **Approve and reject:** steward only, and approve can't be done by the opener or editor. Approve freezes the live figure (no statement binding).
- **Void of a SETTLED claim:** steward only, within 7 days of the first SETTLED log date. The audit records `reversed=`. While the sheet has a list of void reasons, a void must name one.
- **Resettle:** steward only. Re-freezes at `openShownOf`, i.e. what would be due now as an unbound OPEN claim.
- **Redate:** steward only, OPEN or PENDING claims. Due-by, number and binding stay.
- **Split:** OPEN, not deferred, 0 < amount < the claim's amount. The original claim loses its binding; the new claim gets new terms, due-by and number.
- **Reassign:** by permission matrix (steward by default). Not on SETTLED or VOID claims or corrections. The claim loses its binding and, if numbered, gets a new number.
- **Correction:** a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person, and only corrections may name one.
- **Retirement:** a claim can't be dated after `retiredFrom`, or strictly inside a past retirement (`requireClaimable`).
- **Closed period** (`refuseClosed` on due-by): blocks almost every claim change. Adding a proof is allowed.
- **Soft-close:** fixes the totals, but changes are still allowed and new claims are flagged as late entries.
- **Close, reopen, auto-close:** close and reopen follow the matrix (close: clerk or steward; reopen: steward). Auto-close (`closeOverdue`) runs when today changes, once the period's to-date plus the sheet's grace days has passed. Today changing also releases locks and writes a SNAPSHOT line per person.
- **Statement** (`StatementService.take`): binds each counting claim to its **figure** (without late charge or floor) and unbinds every other claim of the person. It records the due-total and count. It can be taken as of an earlier date, using `SheetAsOf` as the basis. Only a steward can cancel the last statement, which unbinds what it bound.
- **Roles:** `Role` is CLERK, STEWARD or VIEWER. `Action` defines the standing rules (OPEN, SETTLE, VOID, CLOSE: clerk or steward; REASSIGN, REOPEN: steward), and `SheetPermission` can override them. `DelegationService` makes a user a steward for a date range. Several things are hard-wired to the steward role: redate, resettle, approve, reject, late void, merge, transfer, clone, archive. `ViewerGuard`, `SheetArchivedGuard` and `AsOfGuard` refuse every write; bulk actions instead report each claim as refused.
- **Imports and bulk actions:**
  - Person import (`PersonImportService`): all-or-nothing. A matching name or alias updates that person, with the grade taking effect from today.
  - Rate import: all-or-nothing.
  - Claim paste: all-or-nothing, adds DRAFTs, and a trailing `#ref` in the note becomes the reference.
  - Quick-add: creates the person with grade A if new.
  - Plan generate: each claim is added on its own, and refused dates are retried next time.
  - Bulk settle: all-or-nothing, and creates a batch (BATCH_SETTLED).
  - Bulk open, move and redate: claim by claim.
- **Dated settings** (`DatedSettings`): defaults are floor 1.00, late 0.00%, terms 14. Floor, late %, terms and the proof and note thresholds use the value in force on the **claim's date**; the clerk limit and cap use the value on the **sheet's today**.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard. The server side is reasonably central and well commented: `RollupService` for the figures and `ClaimService` for the rules. But the figures the screen actually shows are **re-implemented in TypeScript**, spread over a 2,350-line `people.ts`, `rates.service.ts` and `claims.service.ts`. The same "counts / due / late charge / rounding / period-at-end" logic also appears in `PeriodService` and `StatementService`/`SheetAsOf`. So each rule exists two or three times, and a new developer has to cross-check them. That is how I found the small drifts noted above: the claimed-total comment, retired-flag vs retirement-date, and holds judged by claim date for totals but by today for pool cuts.
